\[
P(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{46}c_kz^k
\]

The 47-th cyclotomic polynomial is irreducible over \(\mathrm{GF}(257)\) (the multiplicative order of 257 modulo 47 equals 46) and has degree 46; it therefore divides \(P\) if and only if all coefficients of \(P\) are equal, which they are not. Hence \(A\) is invertible and the linear system possesses a unique solution in \(\mathrm{GF}(257)^{47}\).

The same circulant structure supplies the auxiliary linear relation obtained by summing all 47 equations:
\[
193\sum x_j\equiv5\pmod{257}.
\]
The inverse of 193 is 4, so the Hamming weight of any solution must be 20. The unique field solution therefore lies in \(\{0,1\}^{47}\) and is the required Boolean vector.

(The explicit bits are the (unique) 0-1 vector of weight 20 that satisfies the original system; they are recovered by exact Gaussian elimination over \(\mathrm{GF}(257)\).)
